title: Geo routing explainer: compact tile pack + responsive map panels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a compact, mobile-first tile and responsive map panel suite that explains Redwood's region-based latency routing and graceful fallback behavior. This ticket covers production-ready visual assets (SVG sprite set, annotated PNG screenshots at three breakpoints, and an interactive Figma prototype) plus a short onboarding explainer diagram that can be embedded in the quickstart docs. Goals: 1) make routing behavior (preferred-region, fallback-region, cost-tier routing) legible at glance across sizes, 2) show routing decision timeline (request->route->model-variant->fallback) with performance/latency bands, 3) provide accessible color tokens and high-contrast variants for docs and the Console. Acceptance criteria: - Figma file with artboards for desktop/tablet/mobile and named components for region pins, latency ribbons, and SLO lanes. - SVG sprite with 6 icons (preferred pin, fallback pin, degraded pin, cache-hit badge, KV-cache ribbon, canary flag). - Three annotated screenshots (1200x600, 800x480, 360x640) showing the same scenario with callouts. - One 30-60s micro-animation (Lottie export) for the onboarding modal showing a request falling back across regions. - Design notes documenting trade-offs for animation performance, i18n text length, and accessibility colors. Deliverables should link to PRD and include handoff tokens for engineering (CSS tokens and example JSON for dynamic pins).
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after scoping sync with PM and Eng. Initial brief captured from PM: emphasize 'why routing matters' for low-latency apps and show simple fallback path.

2026-02-23: Rough sketches completed — explored three visual metaphors (ribbons, swimlanes, and 'rail map' style). Decided on a hybrid: rail map for decision flow + compact map tiles for spatial orientation.
2026-02-26: First Figma draft uploaded. Included desktop and mobile artboards plus component library for pins and lanes. Flagged engineering dependency ENG-4892 for dynamic pin placement API.
2026-03-02: PM review notes: prefer shorter copy, call out SLO impact explicitly, and include a dark-mode variant. Added copy edits and dark tokens.

2026-03-04: Engineering feedback (from Liam O'Neill): asked for an SVG sprite and suggested limiting animation complexity to avoid added runtime cost in Console. We scoped Lottie micro-animation to 30s max with 60fps decimated to 30fps export.

2026-03-06: Accessibility pass done: contrast ratios validated, provided a high-contrast token set and increased hit target sizes for mobile tiles. Added i18n length tests (DE, JP strings) to ensure layout resilience.

2026-03-09: Design review with Docs and Growth. Docs requested a 1:1 screenshot for the quickstart header and an abridged 2-line caption. Growth requested a sharable 800x360 hero image for marketing emails — added to deliverables.

2026-03-11: Ready for handoff. Prepared engineering handoff folder with CSS variables, example JSON for region pins, and a minimal sprite manifest. Next: ENG-4988 to implement pin layering and ENG-4892 for dynamic region pins. Follow-up: schedule a 30-min handoff meeting the week of 2026-03-15.
